fix.shows: Priya Seetharaman, a professor in the Management Information Systems Group at the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta, reads the revision as a digital project run through the Commission's ERONet platform, and finds it fails tests that a large system rollout is expected to pass. She writes that notices for logical discrepancy were raised centrally by filters such as the gap in age between parent and child and the number of children linked to one parent, although ages on Indian rolls are often approximate, and that a rule coded into the platform, never published by the Commission, decides who must appear for a hearing. She says matching an elector to a parent on the 2002 roll compares family names across decades and scripts without having been tested at scale, citing West Bengal's 2002 rolls, which were in Bengali and were rendered into English, reportedly with machine tools, over 1.3 crore entries flagged there, and counsel's statement to the Supreme Court that more than half the logical discrepancy cases were variations in names. She writes that features changed while the revision was under way, among them de-duplication software the Commission had told the Supreme Court in late 2025 could not be relied on and later switched back on in some States and Union Territories, and a mapping check that made booth level officers redo finished work. She says new ERONet options in October letting registration officers dispose of notice cases without hearings were explained through demonstration videos, and that such instructions often came through video conferences and WhatsApp groups after the software had already been changed to enforce them, so that the software stood in for the written rule. She adds that the online Form 6 carried a declaration on parents and grandparents that is not in the statutory form. On the timetable, she notes that enumeration in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal ran about six weeks with final rolls in February for polls in April, and that West Bengal's final roll was published with over half a crore names still under adjudication.

note: Second reading, 13 November 2026, against the Chennai print page of 13 November read in full. The online page was not fetched. Both quotes are verbatim from the print text, the second ending before the semicolon that follows Commission. The title is right, Professor in the Management Information Systems Group at IIM Calcutta. ERONet, the 1.3 crore, counsel's statement on name variations, the late-2025 statement on de-duplication software, the October ERONet options, the Form 6 declaration, the six weeks in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, February rolls and April polls, and the half a crore under adjudication all match. Four changes were made. The machine rendering of West Bengal's rolls is hedged with reportedly in the article, so the hedge is restored. The software was switched back on in some States and Union Territories, so the Union Territories are added. The article says the October options were explained through demonstration videos and that interim instructions came through video conferences and WhatsApp groups, so the two are separated. The article ends on the Lessig point and the open question of foresight, so the timetable is no longer described as its ending. No dashes, semicolons, colon hinges or banned words are in the summary.
